Attached is a small sample of bad responses and a latency chart (kestrel_latency_20280409.png). We need immediate help — can you roll this back or provide a mitigation? Our customers are seeing timeouts.

Subject: Re: p99 & throughput spike after qv2 — urgent

Quick technical note after preliminary logs (attached kv-logs-20280409.zip):

Observations:
- QV2 introduced a new int8 execution path with a different KV cache layout. For long-session hot routes (the ones Kestrel uses) we're seeing cache fragmentation and extra cache misses at token 0 of some requests, which increases tail-latency.
- There is also a contention pattern on the batching queue when model token-length distribution has high variance (Kestrel's workload has many short + long mixes).
- Some inference outputs look truncated when fallback heuristics interact with streaming/timeout windows — likely due to earlier token stalls.

Immediate mitigations available now:
1) Re-route Kestrel to the qv1 profile (safe fallback) — should restore latency and output behavior within minutes.
2) Temporarily increase autoscale buffer for their Dedicated pool to reduce batching contention (short-term cost).
3) Patch underway: reduce aggressive cache compaction in qv2 and adjust int8 kernel selection for hot-paths (will take a few hours with validation).

Recommendation: do (1) immediately and (2) as a precaution for the next 24h while we push the qv2 patch. I'm attaching the KV logs we pulled.

Vivek
Staff Engineer, Inference Runtime

Attachments: kv-logs-20280409.zip

Marissa
